samples.summary: Read-side truncation becomes permanent deletion on the next write to the table
samples.evidence: `treeNodeToBlock` replaces the rows of a table past `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` with `[]` (crdt-tree.ts:224-229, mirrored in yorkie-doc-store.ts:471-481). The model produced this way is what writes are built from: `YorkieDocStore.updateBlock` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1666-1686) replaces the whole block subtree with `tree.editByPath(blockPath, endPath, buildBlockNode(block))`, and `buildBlockNode` serializes `block.tableData.rows.map(buildRowNode)` recursively (yorkie-doc-store.ts:364-376). So any edit that routes through `updateBlock`/`updateBlockDirect` on an ancestor table (e.g. the cell-range clear at text-editor.ts:4185) writes the truncated subtree back and destroys the rows below the cap in the CRDT. The module doc in table-nesting.ts promises 'degrade, do not vanish' and says the document 'still opens' — it does, but a single subsequent edit turns the read-time degradation into data loss. Reach is contained to documents deeper than 32 nested tables, i.e. the pathological input the cap targets.

searchedFor: grep MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH across the repo — only crdt-tree.ts, table-layout.ts, yorkie-doc-store.ts, index.ts, tests
samples.summary: The nesting cap is enforced only on read, never on write, so this editor can author past it and lose the content on reload
samples.evidence: `Doc.insertTableInCell` inserts a nested table with no depth check, and its only caller (view/editor.ts:4237) does not check either. Nothing in the repo references `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` outside the two readers, the layout and the tests. A document authored past the cap (tedious but possible one level at a time, or arrived at via paste/DOCX import) reads back truncated at depth 32 and — per the finding above — is then written back truncated. A guard at the insert site would make the cap symmetric.

Both exits do `if (!targetCell) return undefined;` and then `focus: { blockId: targetCell.blocks[0].id, offset: 0 }` (text-editor.ts:3975-3982 and 3995-4001). A cell whose `blocks` array is empty throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id')` from inside a mousedown/mousemove handler, aborting the gesture. The surrounding code is otherwise defensive (`?.` on the row, `if (!innerTableData)`), so the inconsistency looks unintentional; the model normally guarantees one block per cell, which is why I grade the reach as contained.

samples.summary: Shift+click now reaches a throwing `doc.getBlock()` it never reached before
samples.evidence: `resolveCellGesture` calls `this.doc.getBlock(anchorTableId)` (3965) and `this.doc.getBlock(resolveTableId)` (3989). `Doc.getBlock` throws `Block not found: <id>` (model/document.ts:239) rather than returning undefined. The drag path always did this, but the shift+click branch it now shares (text-editor.ts:2093-2095) previously only called `resolveOffsetInCell`, which cannot throw. A stale `anchorCellInfo.tableBlockId` (the parent map is only rebuilt at layout time, and a peer can have removed the table since) therefore turns a shift+click into an uncaught exception in the mousedown handler instead of a caret move. `findBlock`/`?.` would keep the fallback branch reachable.

samples.summary: Copy and paint disagree on the column bound for a ragged table — the exact 'what is copied is what is painted' invariant this change states
samples.evidence: `normalizeCellRange` derives `maxCol` as `rows.reduce((m, r) => Math.max(m, r.cells.length), table.columnWidths.length) - 1` (selection.ts:136-138), i.e. it allows columns beyond `columnWidths.length`. `buildCellRangeRects` clamps painting to `tl.columnXOffsets.length - 1` (selection.ts:728), which is exactly `columnWidths.length - 1`. For a table whose rows carry more cells than `columnWidths` (possible from a peer-written tree: `cols` and the cell children are independent attributes), `getSelectedText` (838-840) and `getSelectedTableCells` (text-editor.ts:4337-4339) walk columns that are never highlighted, so the clipboard contains cells the user never saw selected.

samples.summary: A sibling consumer of the same cell-range data still uses `Math.max(0, ...rows.map(...))`, the RangeError the new code explicitly avoids
samples.evidence: selection.ts:134-135 adds a comment explaining that `Math.max(...rows)` throws `RangeError` past ~100k arguments 'and the row count is a peer's to choose', and folds instead. `visitCellRectangleSlices` computes `Math.max(0, ...rows.map((row) => row.cells.length)) - 1` over the same peer-influenced row array, on the style-write path (`range-runs.ts:81` → `Doc.applyInlineStyleToCells`). Pre-existing and outside the diff, but it is the same hazard the diff names, left open one file away.

samples.summary: Cell-range delete dereferences `rows[cr.start.rowIndex]` unguarded, and the new clamp guarantees index 0 for a zero-row table
samples.evidence: `const firstCell = block.tableData.rows[cr.start.rowIndex].cells[cr.start.colIndex];` has no `?.`, unlike the loop two lines above it (`rows[r]?.cells[c]`). With the new `clampCellIndex`, a table whose `rows.length === 0` yields `max = -1 → Math.max(max, 0) = 0`, so `start.rowIndex` is forced to 0 and `rows[0]` is `undefined` → TypeError while deleting. Requires a cell rectangle naming an empty table (stale range or peer-emptied rows), so the reach is contained, but the clamp makes index 0 the guaranteed outcome rather than an accident.

samples.summary: `normalizeCellRange`'s doc comment misdescribes the unresolved-table case
samples.evidence: The comment says 'A rectangle whose table did not resolve is only ordered, as before'. It is not: with `table === undefined`, `maxRow`/`maxCol` are `Infinity`, but `clampCellIndex` still applies `Number.isFinite` (NaN/±Infinity → 0), `Math.trunc` and the `>= 0` floor (selection.ts:106-109), so negative and fractional indices are rewritten in that branch too. Harmless behaviourally — arguably better — but the comment states the opposite of the code, which matters for the next reader reasoning about which paths are bounded.

samples.summary: Reader and layout caps are off by one level from each other
samples.evidence: The reader stops at the table whose `depth >= 32`, yielding 32 fully-read nesting levels (crdt-tree.ts:224-229). The layout is entered with `nestingDepth = 0` for a top-level table and `layoutCellBlocks` recurses with `nestingDepth + 1`, so it lays out 33 levels before the cap fires (table-layout.ts:145, 283-286). The two 'same cap' comments claim symmetry that the accounting does not have. No user-visible effect — the layout is the more permissive of the pair — but the asymmetry will mislead anyone tuning the constant.

finding.summary: `Doc.findBlockInCells` still walks the parent chain by unguarded recursion — the one parent-map walk this PR's cycle-guard sweep missed, and it is reachable from the very copy/cut path the delta fixes
finding.evidence: The delta's premise (repeated verbatim in the new comments in `peer-cursor.ts:122-128` and `selection.ts:120-125`) is that `blockParentMap` chains come from peer-written CRDT ids and can loop. Three view-side walks now carry a `seen` set (`table-layout.ts:488`, `peer-cursor.ts:128`, `selection.ts:132`, plus `text-editor.ts:3894/3919`, `range-slices.ts:81`). `document.ts:261-290` does the same walk by recursion with no visited set: `findBlockInCells(id)` looks up `cellInfo = _blockParentMap.get(id)`, fails to find `cellInfo.tableBlockId` among the top-level/header/footer arrays, and calls `this.findBlockInCells(cellInfo.tableBlockId)` at line 276. On a chain a→b→a this recurses forever and throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` out of `Doc.getBlock`/`findBlock` rather than returning undefined. It is on the same nested-table cell-range flow the delta touches: `text-editor.ts:2861` (`this.doc.getBlock(cr.blockId)` inside `forEachBlockInSelection`), `text-editor.ts:508` (`this.doc.findBlock(rect.blockId)`) and `text-editor.ts:3330` (`this.doc.getBlock(anchorCI.tableBlockId).tableData!`) all hand it an id taken straight from the same map the new guards distrust. Result: an uncaught exception in a copy/cut/keydown handler instead of the graceful `undefined` every guarded site now returns.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `Doc.findBlockInCells` walks the `_blockParentMap` parent chain by recursion with no visited set, citing an unguarded `this.findBlockInCells(cellInfo.tableBlockId)` call. The code is not as described. At packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:271-274 the signature is `findBlockInCells(blockId: string, seen: Set<string> = new Set([blockId]))` — a visited set seeded with the starting id. The recursion at line 288 is gated by `if (!tableBlock && !seen.has(cellInfo.tableBlockId))`, line 289 adds the id to `seen`, and line 290 threads the set into the recursive call. Lines 261-269 carry an explicit comment describing this as the same cycle guard the view-side walks use, for the same peer-written-CRDT-id reason the finding cites. Tracing the finding's own a→b→a case: the call starts with seen={a}, steps to b (adding it), then at b the map yields a, `seen.has('a')` is true so recursion stops; `tableBlock` stays undefined and control falls through to the fallback at lines 301-303. That fallback, `walkCellsForBlock` (document.ts:75-89), recurses over the concrete document object tree (tableData.rows[].cells[].blocks), not over the parent map, so it cannot follow a synthetic id loop and is bounded. The result for a looping chain is `undefined` — exactly the graceful outcome the finding says is missing — with `getBlock` (line 239) turning that into its normal `Block not found` error rather than a RangeError. Grep shows a single definition of `findBlockInCells` and only two call sites (document.ts:236 in `getBlock`, document.ts:254 in `findBlock`), so the downstream copy/cut and cell-range callers named in the finding all funnel through this one guarded implementation; there is no unguarded variant for them to reach.
